newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-May 26.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-May 26.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
** The ruling United Front coalition discusses possibility of raising the domestic prices of some petroleum products on Sunday but takes no decision

"The main issue discussed was petroleum. No decision has been taken. Several chief ministers were not there. There could be another meeting," a senior United Front leader, who asked not to be identified, told reporters
** The impending increase in government-controlled oil prices has pushed Indian refiner shares higher but analysts now say they are advising caution
An increase in oil prices will not boost profits for the refiners because their earnings are pegged at a government-set formula of 12 percent post-tax return on employed funds
** Indian stocks will continue to drift this week with an eye on the much-delayed petrol price hike

** India's annual monsoon, crucial to farming and the health of the overall economy, is likely to yield a normal amount of rainfall for the 10th successive year in 1997, the Meteorological Department says
The department says in a statement that nine of 16 measures used to predict the monsoon were favourable and "there is a very good probability of a normal monsoon this year"
** Shares of India's largest private steel maker TISCO seen lower as speculators continue to hammer the price after the firm announces a fall in net profit for the year ended March 31, 1997
TISCO's net falls to 4.69 billion rupees, from 5.66 billion in 1995/96
** Earnings announcements expected from refiner Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd and integrated petrochemicals firm Indian Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd
** Foreign investors seen on the sidelines as UK and U.S. stock markets remain closed for Memorial day
** UBS Securities says free liquidity is likely to boost Indian stock markets, the Economic Times says
A report by the securities firm forecasts a surge in portfolio inflows due to high yields on gilts and the higher ceiling on foreign shareholding announced in the federal budget.
** Bombay's benchmark stocks index ends the week 24.41 points lower at 3706.37
